value: [{"pageNumber":80,"summary":"This document, an update to the Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies dated May 31, 2024, highlights the successful results of decisive policy actions, restoring macroeconomic stability. Key achievements include a sustained fiscal surplus, increased international reserves, reduced inflation, and improved market indicators. The government has also increased support for vulnerable populations, such as young mothers and children, and adopted a new pension formula to protect purchasing power. The document emphasizes strong program ownership, with overperformance on end-March performance criteria, but acknowledges the road ahead remains challenging, requiring evolving policies to ensure durability."},{"pageNumber":81,"summary":"Economic activity appears to be stabilizing, with indicators suggesting a bottoming of real wages for formal sector workers and a recovery in agricultural production. The disinflation process is rapid, with monthly inflation at 8.8% in April and core inflation trending lower. The central bank's balance sheet is strengthening, supported by declining policy interest rates and sterilized reserve purchases. FX realignment has led to external surpluses and significant reserve accumulation, exceeding program targets. The goods trade surplus reached approximately US$15.5 billion from December to April, driven by import compression and export volume rebound."},{"pageNumber":82,"summary":"Prudent public debt management has facilitated net placements and reduced rollover risks, including a successful debt exchange extending 40% of outstanding peso debt. New short-term fixed-rate instruments aim to shift liquidity from BCRA's overnight facilities and maintain net-zero monetary financing. Domestic arrears have been kept below the program ceiling after clearing inherited arrears. Efforts to deregulate and create a market-based economy continue, with corrections in regulated utility prices, fuel prices reflecting international comparators, and elimination of wheat price subsidies. The Emergency Decree (DNU) is improving resource allocation."},{"pageNumber":83,"summary":"Inflation is projected to converge to around 4% monthly by end-2024, with further declines expected. This is supported by a strong fiscal anchor, an end to debt monetization, and a strengthened monetary and FX policy framework, which will foster peso demand in a 'currency competition' regime. The external current account is expected to shift from a deficit to a surplus of 0.6% of GDP this year, driven by demand compression and expenditure switching. External surpluses are projected long-term, with reserve accumulation expected to increase by US$7 billion this year."},{"pageNumber":84,"summary":"The government commits to adapting economic policies to changing circumstances to meet program objectives, safeguarding policy credibility through a strong fiscal anchor and reserve accumulation goals. Contingency measures include strengthening excises (especially fuels), accelerating subsidy reductions (energy and transportation), streamlining transfers, and enhancing tax administration and expenditure controls. On monetary and FX policy, the government is ready to adjust to meet disinflation and reserve accumulation goals. If inflation proves challenging, the ex-ante real policy interest rate will be raised sooner to support peso demand, accompanied by clear policy communication."},{"pageNumber":85,"summary":"Fiscal policy aims for overall balance this year by improving tax progressivity and efficiency, reducing subsidies, and strengthening expenditure controls while safeguarding social assistance. Subsidies for electricity and gas are being raised to achieve full cost recovery for most users by S2:2024, replacing the current segmentation scheme with one supporting only vulnerable households' basic energy needs. A decree removing the CVS formula for electricity and gas bills has been issued as a prior action. These measures will reduce energy and transport subsidies by at least 0.7% of GDP."},{"pageNumber":86,"summary":"The government plans to enhance the tax system's efficiency, equity, and simplicity by October 2024, aiming to reduce distortive taxes like 'impuesto pais' by end-2024. Complementary reforms will focus on pension system sustainability, fiscal frameworks, and intergovernmental transfers. A roadmap for these reforms will be developed by end-2024. Regarding financing, the government will continue to tap the domestic debt market to refinance maturing debt in 2024, offering a menu of instruments and maturities, and eventually providing an auction calendar. FX- and inflation-linked bonds will be replaced with fixed-rate securities."},{"pageNumber":87,"summary":"The overnight policy interest rate will continue to guide inflation and inflation expectations, evolving to address quasi-fiscal deficits and support disinflation within FX controls and a strong fiscal anchor. The real policy rate is expected to turn positive later in the year to support peso demand as FX controls ease and private credit recovers. Plans are underway to extend monetary operations to include Treasuries to help establish the short end of the yield curve. The BCRA will refrain from profit transfers to the Treasury, and accounting standards will be refined to international norms. FX policy will become more flexible to sustain reserve buildup and disinflation."},{"pageNumber":88,"summary":"A proposed law, expected for Congressional approval, aims to support private formal employment, incentivize long-term investments, strengthen the hydrocarbon sector, streamline regulatory costs, and rationalize state-owned enterprises (SOEs), including clarifying privatization processes. Upon approval, focus will shift to implementing regulations. Efforts will also continue to improve efficiency and investment incentives in key sectors like energy and communications, and to unwind cross-subsidies. Improving governance and combating corruption remain central, including strengthening the AML/CFT framework and approving pending reforms to Law 25.24."},{"pageNumber":89,"summary":"This page contains 'Table 1. Technical Memorandum of Understanding Update' dated May 31, 2024, outlines the definitions for performance criteria (PCs) and indicative targets (ITs) under the Extended Arrangement. It details the methods for assessing program performance and the information required for monitoring. Crucially, it defines 'program exchange rates' as those prevailing on December 29, 2023, for all foreign currency-related evaluations, except for items affecting fiscal balances, which use current exchange rates. Text Table 1 lists these program exchange rates."},{"pageNumber":95,"summary":"This section defines the primary balance of the federal government according to the 'Esquema IMIG' and 2014 GFS Manual practices. It details revenue inclusions (tax, property, other current, capital) and exclusions (financial transfers from the Central Bank, interest from intra-public sector holdings, asset sale proceeds, license/permit revenue, debt issuance revenue, SDRs) for primary deficit calculations. This page also begins defining terms related to debt and other financial concepts relevant to the program's monitoring framework."},{"pageNumber":96,"summary":"This page details the measurement and monitoring of the Federal government's primary balance, which is a cumulative value from the start of the calendar year. It then defines domestic arrears as floating debt, calculated as the difference between accrual and cash basis primary spending, including intra-public transfers and various spending categories. A specific ceiling is set for the daily average of domestic arrears over the final two weeks of each quarter (0.8% of GDP). Daily data on arrears and underlying spending will be provided to the Fund."},{"pageNumber":97,"summary":"This section defines Gross official reserve liabilities in foreign currencies for program monitoring. It includes liabilities with original maturity of one year or less, Fund disbursements (net of program financing and payments), and net deliverable forward FX liabilities. It clarifies that the Federal government's foreign liabilities and FX deposits at the BCRA are excluded. Various liabilities like swaps with China, bank reserve requirements, SEDESA, ALADI, and non-resident deposits are considered BCRA liabilities. The measurement is the cumulative change in Net International Reserves (NIR) from December 10, 2023, monitored daily."},{"pageNumber":98,"summary":"This page defines the ceiling on the BCRA's Net Financing of the Federal Government. It includes various forms of financing such as overdrafts, profit distributions, government debt acquisition (primary, secondary, direct), and issuance of non-marketable bonds. Net financing is defined after deducting cash transfers from the government to the BCRA for repurchasing securities, reducing overdrafts, or recapitalizing the BCRA. Transactions related to debt exchanges or rollovers of non-marketable bonds are excluded. The cumulative flow ceiling for net financing in 2024 is set at zero."},{"pageNumber":99,"summary":"This section provides detailed definitions of debt for program purposes, including obligations like repurchase agreements, official swap arrangements, suppliers' credits, and leases. It specifies that arrears, penalties, and damages arising from failure to make payment on debt obligations are considered debt. However, failure to make payments on obligations not classified as debt (e.g., payment on delivery) does not create debt. The definition of external debt is consistent with the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual. This section clarifies what constitutes debt under the program's framework."}]
